facts: Wombats dig burrows with their strong claws, and spend the hottest part of the day resting underground.
A wombat's pouch faces backwards, so no soil gets in while it digs.
Wombats mostly eat native grasses, sedges and roots.
Wombats get most of the water they need from their food, so they don't drink often.
Wombats are mostly active at night, at dusk and at dawn.
Invasive plants crowd out the native grasses that wombats rely on.
